name: MCP Apps (SEP-1865)
tagline: MCP extension: tools ship sandboxed HTML UIs into chat hosts

other.label: fka.dev: MCP Apps Should Work in the Terminal Too (2026-09-09)
Claude Code issue #93973: plugin API for interactive TUI elements
Anthropic: donating MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation

license.notes: Repo LICENSE: MCP is transitioning MIT -> Apache-2.0; new code/spec contributions Apache-2.0, docs CC-BY-4.0, un-relicensed older contributions stay MIT (GitHub reports NOASSERTION; npm package still declares MIT). MCP-UI is Apache-2.0.

language: Spec + TypeScript SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps); Views are HTML/JS
backing: Model Context Protocol project, governed under the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation directed fund co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI, Dec 2025). SEP authors from MCP-UI (Ido Salomon, Liad Yosef), Anthropic and OpenAI among others.

adoption.summary: The de facto standard for UI inside chat hosts: Claude and ChatGPT both render it, and it unifies MCP-UI and OpenAI's Apps SDK. Star count understates adoption; the spec repo is small but the SDK has 4.6M weekly downloads.

maintainability.recent_activity: 56 commits on ext-apps main since 2026-07-11; MCP-UI shows no main-branch commits in that window (last client release 7.1.1, 2026-05-09)
maintainability.bus_factor: high: foundation-governed, multiple vendors depend on it
maintainability.summary: Stable spec, active SDK, neutral governance; MCP-UI (the community predecessor) has gone quiet as the official extension took over.

architecture.summary: A tool declares a ui:// resource (text/html;profile=mcp-app) in _meta.ui.resourceUri; when the model calls the tool, the host fetches the HTML and renders it in a sandboxed iframe (often via a sandbox proxy). The View talks to the host over JSON-RPC on postMessage using MCP's own message shapes: ui/initialize, ui/notifications/tool-input(-partial), tool-result, tool-cancelled, size-changed, host-context-changed; the View can call server tools through the host, send ui/message, ui/open-link, ui/request-display-mode and ui/update-model-context. Hosts theme Views through standardized CSS variables and enforce CSP declared by the server.
key_points: UI is code (HTML/JS), not a declarative tree; security comes from iframe sandboxing, CSP, predeclared resources and auditable JSON-RPC
Bidirectional: host pushes tool input/result; View calls tools and updates model context
Display modes (inline/fullscreen/pip) and container sizing negotiated
Wire protocol unchanged between SDK 1.x and 2.x

No terminal host renders MCP Apps; fka.dev proposes a parallel JSON terminal view (vendor extension dev.fka/terminal-ui, A2UI-shaped createSurface/updateComponents/updateDataModel, catalog ids, state bindings, named actions)
Claude Code #93973 (opened 2026-09-13, open, unassigned) asks for plugin TUI slots: keybinding actions, read access to rendered messages with ids, overlay/side-panel slot with clicks

performance.summary: No published performance numbers; a View is an ordinary web page so its rendering/update rate is whatever the browser and the app code achieve.

agent_usability.how: Indirect: the model calls an MCP tool and the host shows that tool's View. The View, not the model, drives the UI; it can call tools and push context to the model (ui/update-model-context).
agent_usability.integration_effort: Write an MCP server that registers tools with UI resources (SDK + agent skills such as create-mcp-app); works in any compliant host without host changes.
agent_usability.readback: Only what the View chooses to report via ui/update-model-context or tool calls; the model cannot query the DOM or see the render.
agent_usability.granular_edits: No addressing: the host delivers tool inputs/results; the View app decides what to change.
agent_usability.summary: Gives agents a way to ship arbitrary rich UI into the chat, but the UI is an opaque app the model neither inspects nor edits.

score_notes.ui_as_data: The resource is a declared, reviewable HTML document, but the UI itself is code.
score_notes.agent_drivable: Model triggers Views via tool calls and gets tool calls back; it cannot directly manipulate a live View.
score_notes.readback: Structured but voluntary: whatever the View sends via update-model-context.
score_notes.live_data_rate: A View can open its own connections so data bypasses the model; no published numbers.
score_notes.terminal_native: HTML-only; terminal views exist only as a 2026-09 blog proposal.
score_notes.pixel_graphics: Full web platform (canvas, WebGL; Three.js and ShaderToy examples).
score_notes.maturity: Stable spec shipped in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Goose; not yet ubiquitous across MCP clients.

steelman: MCP Apps is where the users already are. It turned MCP-UI's community experiment and OpenAI's Apps SDK into one stable, foundation-governed standard, and Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code and Goose render it today, so one server reaches hundreds of millions of chat users with a real interactive app, not a widget catalog. It refuses to invent a UI language: a View is just HTML, so anything the web can draw (maps, 3D, sheet music, Excalidraw) works, and safety comes from proven browser isolation (sandboxed iframes, CSP, predeclared resources, auditable JSON-RPC over MCP's own messages). With 4.6M weekly SDK downloads and agent skills that scaffold an app in one prompt, it is the default answer to 'my tool needs a UI'.
weaknesses: UI is opaque code: the model cannot read back, address or patch it; agent sees only what the View reports
HTML-only; no terminal host renders it (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI) and terminal views are only a blog proposal
Security relies on iframe sandboxing of arbitrary code, the opposite of A2UI's 'data not code' stance
MCP-UI predecessor now quiet; hosts differ in support (README: 'Host support varies')

relation_to_scene.overlap: Both put an interactive UI in front of a user on an agent's behalf and let the UI call back into the agent's tools.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Nothing in the UI model; scene's tooling should reuse MCP itself as the transport rather than a private socket protocol for remote agents.
borrow: Expose scene as an MCP server (push/patch/keys/screen/state tools) so any MCP agent can drive it
Use the fka.dev extension shape: advertise a terminal-view resource next to HTML, negotiate catalogs in initialize capabilities
ui/update-model-context pattern: let the UI push a compact state summary to the model
CSP/predeclared-resource idea as a template for scene's command allowlist policy
relation_to_scene.gap_left: A terminal renderer for MCP tool UIs. scene could be the host-side terminal view the fka.dev proposal and Claude Code #93973 are asking for, with readback and patching MCP Apps doesn't offer.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: MCP Apps owns UI in web chat hosts; scene can fill the terminal gap and speak MCP as its control transport.
